analysis:
Examined head text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md lines 397-1301. The changed ranges in this batch are documentation only. Line 156 adds an `addon` command table row. Lines 904-932 add a new `darkbloom addon` section covering status, hold and release, with `--force` for release. Line 3 changes the date, and line 1758 lies outside these units.

The new section documents an operator-only debug control. It reaches the running provider through the owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to the live process identity (lines 909-911). Add-ons use a separate local socket (docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md).

Security-relevant claims:
- A hold closes admission, finishes accepted work for up to 120 s, and unloads every model (line 922).
- `release --force` can resume serving while an add-on's VMs may still use memory (line 924). This is an operator availability/memory choice, not a confidentiality issue.
- Providers without add-on support are refused before anything is sent (lines 927-928).

The operator is already the TB-003 adversary with full local control, so operator-invoked holds add no privilege beyond existing stop/drain. Holds affect only availability (cf. T-010/T-029-style DoS by the operator, already within TB-003).

Integration should verify against provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/AddonCommand.swift and ProviderCore/Addon/ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift (`handleAddonControl`), which are not supplied here. Four points to check:
- The mailbox is actually owner-only and bound to the process identity.
- The add-on local socket (addon-hold-ipc.md) authenticates its peers. A non-owner local process able to place holds would be a DoS surface not modelled in the threat model; the threat model has no TB for add-on IPC.
- Release/drain interacts correctly with lifecycle drain and authorization state (T-053).
- The 120 s accepted-work deadline does not drop terminal usage/billing.

No code is visible in this batch, so no regression is cited. The threat model may need a boundary entry for add-on hold IPC if that code is new in this PR.
